questionsToConsider: Do the section names in the grid match what readers see on your contents page?
Are you deciding something specific, like dropping a section or changing frequency, that deserves its own question?
Should print and digital readers be asked different questions about the reading experience?
Do you want readers to be able to volunteer for interviews or contribute stories?
guide.howToUseResponses: Read the section grid first: sections most readers skip are candidates for a rethink, and those read by long-time readers but skipped by new ones may need a better introduction. Put the favourite pieces and the disappointments side by side, since the patterns in each tell editors what to do more and less of. Keep an eye on readers who say they probably will not keep reading and what they wrote about why.
customizeSteps: Rename the grid rows to your real sections and adjust the topics list to your beat.
Change the format options to the ways your magazine is actually published, such as a newsletter edition or podcast.
Put the link in the next issue, on the website and in subscriber emails, then compare answers from print and digital readers in the dashboard.

faqs.q: What should a magazine reader survey ask?
faqs.a: How people read, how much of each issue they get through, which sections they read or skip, what they want more of, and whether they plan to keep reading.

faqs.q: How often should a magazine run a reader survey?
faqs.a: Once a year is enough for most publications, plus a short one when you are about to make a big change such as a redesign.

faqs.q: How do I get more readers to respond?
faqs.a: Tell them their answers will shape the next issues, keep it short and share the link in several places. A chat that asks one question at a time also feels less like homework.

faqs.q: Can I use this survey for a newsletter or blog?
faqs.a: Yes, with a few edits to the format and section names. For email newsletters there is also a dedicated newsletter feedback survey.
